text: The E1024 integration slice asserts the document in rwb_document through the P5 document contract, the case through the P3 case contract and the party key through the P1 customer contract; the decision record is read on the shared topic rwb.decision-record.v1, and the central ledger belongs to RWB-ITG-E1027-ITG. The suite reads no service schema and no P5 operation is assumed to return a case or party link.
why: The legacy story reads the case and writes the decision log in-process, while the target splits the document, the case and the decision record across P5, P3, P1 and P7, and the WP lists P1, P3 and P5 only.
read: RWB-E1-024 sections 4, 11 and 12; Architecture v5 slides 16, 41 and 42; DP-01, DP-03; Ownership Map P1, P3, P5, P7
impact: The document, case and party assertions are composed from three owner contracts; the ledger assertion is deferred to E1027 and no field is invented.

text: The document type version in force is read through the P5 document contract and every field definition in force is checked against the P1 data-dictionary contract; the load and the approval are exercised by the P3 reference-data and P5 APP stories, and the DOCUMENT_TYPE rows stay in rwb_document.
why: The legacy P4 reference-load endpoint and the LOV list service move to P3 under DP-07, and the WP lists P1 and P5 only.
read: RWB-E1-025 sections 3, 4, 11 and 12; Architecture v5 slides 15 and 16; DP-01, DP-07; Ownership Map P3, P5
impact: The load is asserted through the owner's contract only; the four-eyes approval is not re-implemented in the suite and no business value is invented.

text: SCR-30 is a gateway-bff composite route over the P5 case document list, the P5 document type read and the P3 parameter and reference-data contracts; the upload, the search and the checklist are asserted through that composite and through the P5 contract, and the scan is asserted by its result only.
why: The legacy screen calls the document endpoints directly, and the target route and its aggregation shape are not published in the Ownership Map.
read: RWB-E1-026 sections 4 and 12; Architecture v5 slide 16 and slide 20; DP-06, DP-07, DP-19
impact: The screen is proved through one composite route; the scan internals are not asserted and no P5 internal path is assumed.

text: The E1027 suite writes decision records through the PLT decision-record library conformance caller in a real transaction and asserts them in the P7 central ledger and on rwb.decision-record.v1; decision codes and LOV values are held by P3 in the target and are asserted as the values in force, and no data-lake copy exists.
why: The WP lists the PLT library and P7 only, while the legacy story reads P4 lists and shared parameters and the target moves them to P3 (DP-06, DP-07); the lake copy is retired (DP-17).
read: RWB-E1-027 sections 3, 4, 11 and 12; Architecture v5 slides 14, 27 and 42; DP-03, DP-06, DP-07, DP-17
impact: The writer and the ledger are proved end to end; the P3 parameter and LOV reads are proved in the P3 stories and are not duplicated in this suite.

text: The service-level and prescription clocks are durable Temporal timers inside CaseWorkflow, read through the P3 timer projection and proved through TimerBreached on rwb.case.events.v1 and the P7 decision log; JOB-05, TimerDue and Quartz are retired, the wave 1 deviation pause is triggered through the P3 case action contract, and the P1 account-date and holiday inputs are exercised by RWB-P3-E1028-APP and not called by this suite.
why: ASM-A6-tables-12 keeps the timer row as a P3 projection and moves the clock to Temporal, the WP lists P3, P4 and P7 only, and the deviation service is wave 2.
read: RWB-E1-028 sections 3, 4 and 12; Architecture v5 slides 42 and 44; Temporal and Drools design slides 13 and 24; ASM-A6-tables-12
impact: The timer, breach and decision assertions use the P3 projection and the P3 event only; the P1 inputs and the wave 2 deviation event are not duplicated, and the retired JOB-05 is not asserted.
